subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should OpenClaw add a plugin user-prompt replacement contract, and should it live on before_prompt_build with legacy before_agent_start compatibility or on modifying llm_input?
rationale: The request adds a public plugin capability to rewrite model-bound user input, so automation should not choose the hook layer, precedence, audit behavior, or prompt-injection trust boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add prompt-build replacement
options.body: Add a documented replacement field to before_prompt_build, carry it through legacy before_agent_start, enforce allowPromptInjection filtering, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

options.title: Route through LLM interception
options.body: Defer this issue to an llm_input-style modifying hook if maintainers want prompt rewriting at the provider-boundary instead of the prompt-build boundary.

options.title: Keep hooks additive-only
options.body: Reject prompt replacement and direct oversized-prompt mitigation to context-engine, memory, blocking, or provider-side controls.

recommendation.title: Add prompt-build replacement
recommendation.body: Add a documented replacement field to before_prompt_build, carry it through legacy before_agent_start, enforce allowPromptInjection filtering, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history across shared prompt hooks and harness parity, making him the best available owner for the cross-runner API decision.
